events.label: Holmes presents papers about the Gloria Scott case

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I have some papers here which I really think, Watson, that it would be worth your while to glance over. These are the documents in the extraordinary case of the Gloria Scott, and this is the message which struck Justice of the Peace Trevor dead with horror when he read it.

events.label: Holmes takes a cylinder from a drawer and hands Watson a note
The note states its message

communicates.speaker: short_note
communicates.content: The supply of game for London is going steadily up. Head-keeper Hudson, we believe, has been now told to receive all orders for fly-paper and for preservation of your hen-pheasant's life.

events.label: Watson reads the note and Holmes chuckles at his expression
Watson asks why Holmes said he should study the case

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: But why did you say just now that there were very particular reasons why I should study this case?

events.label: Holmes says this was the first case he was ever engaged in

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Because it was the first in which I was ever engaged.

events.label: Holmes sits forward and spreads the documents on his knees
Holmes asks Watson about Victor Trevor

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You never heard me talk of Victor Trevor?

events.label: Holmes describes Victor Trevor as his only college friend
Victor Trevor invites Holmes to his father's place and Holmes accepts
Holmes describes Old Trevor and Donnithorpe
Victor Trevor's father discusses his life and responds to Holmes's deductions

communicates.speaker: old_trevor
communicates.content: Come, now, Mr. Holmes. I'm an excellent subject, if you can deduce anything from me.

events.label: Holmes says Trevor has gone about in fear of a personal attack

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I might suggest that you have gone about in fear of some personal attack within the last twelve months.

events.label: Old Trevor acknowledges Holmes's deduction and explains the reason for his caution

communicates.speaker: old_trevor
communicates.content: Well, that's true enough. When we broke up that poaching gang, they swore to knife us, and Sir Edward Holly has actually been attacked. I've always been on my guard since then, though I have no idea how you know it.

events.label: Holmes says Trevor's stick has been modified into a weapon

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You have a very handsome stick. By the inscription I observed that you had not had it more than a year. But you have taken some pains to bore the head of it and pour melted lead into the hole so as to make it a formidable weapon. I argued that you would not take such precautions unless you had some danger to fear.

events.label: Holmes says Trevor boxed in his youth and points to his ears as evidence

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You have boxed a good deal in your youth. No. It is your ears. They have the peculiar flattening and thickening which marks the boxing man.

events.label: Holmes says Trevor dug for money, visited New Zealand, and visited Japan

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You have done a good deal of digging by your callosities. You have been in New Zealand. You have visited Japan.

events.label: Holmes says Trevor was closely associated with someone whose initials were J. A.

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You have been most intimately associated with some one whose initials were J. A., and whom you afterwards were eager to entirely forget.

events.label: Old Trevor faints and is then revived
Holmes describes how he recognized the tattooed initials and their attempted removal

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: When you bared your arm to draw that fish into the boat I saw that J. A. had been tattooed in the bend of the elbow. The letters were still legible, but it was perfectly clear from their blurred appearance, and from the staining of the skin round them, that efforts had been made to obliterate them. It was obvious, then, that those initials had once been very familiar to you, and that you had afterwards wished to forget them.

events.label: Victor Trevor speaks in relief and ends the discussion of the initials

communicates.speaker: victor_trevor
communicates.content: What an eye you have! It is just as you say. But we won't talk of it. Of all ghosts the ghosts of our old lovers are the worst. Come into the billiard-room and have a quiet cigar.

communicates.speaker: hudson
communicates.content: There was a man at the door who wanted to see Mr. Trevor. He would not give any. He says that you know him, and that he only wants a moment's conversation.

communicates.speaker: victor_trevor

events.label: Watson asks what the matter is

events.label: Victor Trevor says the governor has apoplexy and nervous shock and may not be found alive

communicates.content: Apoplexy. Nervous shock, He's been on the verge all day. I doubt if we shall find him alive.

events.label: Watson asks what caused the governor's condition

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: What caused it?

events.label: Victor Trevor says the evening visitor was the devil himself

communicates.speaker: victor_trevor
communicates.content: It was the devil, Holmes. Yes, it was the devil himself. We have not had a peaceful hour since—not one. The governor has never held up his head from that evening, and now the life has been crushed out of him and his heart broken, all through this accursed Hudson. Ah, that is what I would give so much to know. The kindly, charitable, good old governor—how could he have fallen into the clutches of such a ruffian! But I am so glad that you have come, Holmes. I trust very much to your judgment and discretion, and I know that you will advise me for the best.

events.label: Trevor and his companion travel along the country road toward the squire's dwelling

communicates.speaker: hudson
communicates.content: My father made the fellow gardener, and then, as that did not satisfy him, he was promoted to be butler. The house seemed to be at his mercy, and he wandered about and did what he chose in it. The maids complained of his drunken habits and his vile language. The dad raised their wages all round to recompense them for the annoyance.

events.label: Hudson takes the boat and his father's best gun for shooting trips

communicates.content: I've had enough of Norfolk. I'll run down to Mr. Beddoes in Hampshire. He'll be as glad to see me as you were, I daresay.

communicates.speaker: old_trevor
communicates.content: You're not going away in an unkind spirit, Hudson, I hope

communicates.content: Any message for me?

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes

events.label: Trevor brings the papers into the study
Trevor hands over the short note
A warning note is read aloud

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: The game is up. Hudson has told all. Fly for your life.

events.label: Victor Trevor reacts to the warning
Holmes explains the ciphered words in the note

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It means nothing to the message, but it might mean a good deal to us if we had no other means of discovering the sender. You see that he has begun by writing 'The game is,' and so on. Afterwards he had, to fulfill the prearranged cipher, to fill in any two words in each space. He would naturally use the first words which came to his mind, and if there were so many which referred to sport among them, you may be tolerably sure that he is either an ardent shot or interested in breeding.

events.label: Victor Trevor identifies Beddoes as connected with shooting preserves

communicates.speaker: victor_trevor
communicates.content: My poor father used to have an invitation from him to shoot over his preserves every autumn.

events.label: Holmes concludes the note comes from Beddoes

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It is undoubtedly from him that the note comes. It only remains for us to find out what this secret was which the sailor Hudson seems to have held over the heads of these two wealthy and respected men.

events.label: Victor Trevor hands over the statement and asks for it to be read

communicates.speaker: victor_trevor
communicates.content: From you I shall have no secrets. Here is the statement which was drawn up by my father when he knew that the danger from Hudson had become imminent. I found it in the Japanese cabinet, as he told the doctor. Take it and read it to me, for I have neither the strength nor the courage to do it myself.

events.label: Holmes produces and reads the papers

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: These are the very papers, Watson, which he handed to me, and I will read them to you, as I read them in the old study that night to him. They are endorsed outside: 'Some particulars of the voyage of the bark Gloria Scott, from her leaving Falmouth on the 8th October, 1855, to her destruction in N. lat. 15º 20', W. long. 25º 14' on Nov. 6th.' It is in the form of a letter.

events.label: The father’s letter is read

communicates.speaker: old_trevor
communicates.content: My dear, dear son,—Now that approaching disgrace begins to darken the closing years of my life, I can write with all truth and honesty that it is not the terror of the law, it is not the loss of my position in the county, nor is it my fall in the eyes of all who have known me, which cuts me to the heart; but it is the thought that you should come to blush for me—you who love me and who have seldom, I hope, had reason to do other than respect me. But if the blow falls which is forever hanging over me, then I should wish you to read this, that you may know straight from me how far I have been to blame. If by any chance this paper should be still undestroyed and should fall into your hands, I conjure you, by all you hold sacred, by the memory of your dear mother, and by the love which had been between us, to hurl it into the fire and to never give one thought to it again.

clues.significance: Holmes used the note's wording to frame it as the message that struck Justice of the Peace Trevor with horror.
Holmes inferred that the initials had been tattooed in the bend of Trevor's elbow and then had been deliberately blurred and stained in an attempt to obliterate them.
Holmes inferred that every third word of the note would yield a hidden message from the wording of the grey-paper note.
Holmes inferred that the sender had used a prearranged cipher and that the sporting words could identify the sender as a shot or breeder from the note's filled-in phrases.
Holmes inferred that the note came from Beddoes after Victor Trevor said his father had received invitations from Beddoes to shoot over the preserves.
